merger_description:
Redwood Services Group Australia Pty Ltd (**Redwood**) proposes to acquire 100% of the shares in The Virtual IT Department Pty Ltd, The Virtual IT Department (Qld) Pty Ltd and Globechat Communications Australia Pty Ltd (together, **Virtual IT Department**) (the **Acquisition**).

Redwood’s subsidiaries supply managed IT services, including the provision of software and hardware, to small-to-medium businesses and other enterprise customers across Australia. Redwood is part of Evergreen Services Group (**Evergreen**), which acquires managed IT service providers and other technology services companies globally. Evergreen is a portfolio company of Alpine Investors, a private equity firm headquartered in San Francisco, California.

Virtual IT Department supplies managed IT services (including VoIP phone systems and support) to small-to-medium businesses and community sector organisations.

events.title: Notification waiver determination published

determination_table_content.details:
In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information provided in the application, the ACCC
considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material
lessening of competition given:
a. the parties’ combined share in the supply of managed IT
services to customers in Australia is estimated to be low
and the increase in share of supply arising from the
Acquisition would be small
b. there are alternative suppliers of managed IT services to
customers in Victoria, Queensland and across Australia.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s guidance on notification
waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
